title: Rental Benefit Payment Rules and Per-Loss Maximums, Rental Reimbursement Coverage
content:
**Payment rule.** Under Rental Reimbursement Coverage each rental day is paid at the lower of the actual daily charge and the package daily limit; mileage, fuel and damage waivers are not paid, and charges above the limit are the customer's. The rental days paid on a claim, including this payment, never exceed 30 and the amount never exceeds the package maximum for one covered loss. Network agencies are paid directly on weekly invoices; other rentals and ride-hailing or transit fares are reimbursed to the named insured on itemized receipts submitted within 60 days of the rental's end.

## 1. Package figures used in a payment

| Package | Daily limit | Maximum for one covered loss | Most rental days for one covered loss |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cardinal Point Rental Reimbursement $20/$600 | USD 20.00 | USD 600.00 | 30 |
| Cardinal Point Rental Reimbursement $25/$750 | USD 25.00 | USD 750.00 | 30 |
| Cardinal Point Rental Reimbursement $30/$900 | USD 30.00 | USD 900.00 | 30 |
| Cardinal Point Rental Reimbursement $40/$1,200 | USD 40.00 | USD 1200.00 | 30 |
| Cardinal Point Rental Reimbursement $50/$1,500 | USD 50.00 | USD 1500.00 | 30 |
| Cardinal Point Rental Reimbursement $60/$1,800 | USD 60.00 | USD 1800.00 | 30 |

## 2. Amount of one payment

The amount of a payment is the per-day figure — the lower of the actual daily charge and the package daily limit — multiplied by the rental days paid in that payment, the product rounded to the nearest cent, a half cent rounded up.

## 3. The per-claim ceilings

Before a payment is made, the payments already recorded on the same claim number are read from the company's records. Two ceilings apply to the claim, each counting this payment together with those already made:

- the total rental days paid on the claim never exceed 30;
- the total amount paid on the claim never exceeds the package maximum for one covered loss.

Reaching a ceiling exactly is within it; going beyond it by one day or by one cent is not.

## 4. Worked payments (hypothetical inputs)

1. $30/$900 package, actual daily charge USD 34.50, 7 rental days in the invoice period. The per-day figure is the lower of USD 34.50 and USD 30.00, which is USD 30.00; multiplied by 7 the payment is USD 210.00. The USD 4.50 a day above the limit is the customer's.
2. $25/$750 package, actual daily charge USD 22.75, 4 rental days. The per-day figure is USD 22.75; multiplied by 4 the payment is USD 91.00.
3. A claim already has 23 rental days paid. A payment for 7 further days brings the claim to 30 days, which is within the ceiling; a payment for 8 further days would bring it to 31, which exceeds it.
4. On the $20/$600 package a claim already has USD 560.00 paid. A further payment of USD 40.00 brings the claim to USD 600.00, within the maximum; a further payment of USD 60.00 would bring it to USD 620.00, beyond it.

## 5. Who is paid and how

| Rental | Paid to | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Network rental agency | The agency, directly | Weekly invoices |
| Other rental, ride-hailing or transit | The named insured | Itemized receipts submitted within 60 days of the rental's end |
